## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `cmp32` (32-bit registered unsigned comparator: y = (a < b)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module cmp32 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire valid_i,
    input wire [31:0] a_i,
    input wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg valid_o,
    output reg [0:0] y_o
);

wire lt_0 = (a_i[31:0] < b_i[31:0]);
wire eq_0 = (a_i[31:0] == b_i[31:0]);

wire cmp_0 = lt_0;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o <= 1'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;
        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= cmp_0;
    end
end
endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 268.926 um^2, WNS 7.62112 ns, score 75.942274.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 177.156 um^2, WNS 7.69083 ns, estimated score 76.731144 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: Correctness confirmed. Now let's run the full place-and-route to verify the actual improvement.

This nibble-based tree comparator improved the score from 75.942274 to 76.109606 (+0.167332), with slightly better WNS (7.6378 vs 7.62112) and slightly lower area (268.394 vs 268.926). I have 1 place_and_route budget remaining. Given the diminishing returns seen across multiple structural variants (bit-pair tree was worse, subtraction-based was worse, and this nibble tree is the best found), I'll finalize with this result rather than risk the last budget slot on a marginal/uncertain variant.

input.summary: Explored several equivalent restructurings of the 32-bit unsigned comparator (bit-pairwise priority tree, subtraction-based magnitude compare, cleaned-up baseline, and a nibble-granularity priority-encode tree) using estimate_ppa to screen cheaply before spending place_and_route budget. Verified functional equivalence via simulate (including a caught/fixed indexing bug in an early tree attempt) and prove_equivalence (formal sequential equivalence, PROVEN) for the final candidate. The winning design computes per-nibble (4-bit) less-than/equal signals directly via '<' and '==' on 4-bit slices, then combines them with a compact 3-level priority-merge tree (nibble->2-nibble->4-nibble->final) instead of the flat 32-bit '<' operator relied on by the reference. This gave the best measured place_and_route result: area 268.394 um^2 (vs 268.926 baseline), WNS 7.6378 ns (vs 7.62112 baseline), score 76.109606 vs baseline 75.942274 (+0.167332). Other variants (bit-pair binary tree, subtraction-based) scored worse in estimate_ppa and were not submitted to the limited place_and_route budget. This nibble-tree result is the best verified submission and is used as the final score.
